\subsection*{Diagonalization --- NTime Hierarchy: Introduction}

Declarations of the Lean module \texttt{TCSlib.Complexity.Diagonalization.NTimeHierarchy}.

\subsection*{Diagonalization --- NTime Hierarchy: Results}

\begin{theorem}[Timed universal nondeterministic simulation]
\lean{Turing.exists_timed_universal_NDTM}
\label{Turing.exists_timed_universal_NDTM}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.CodeNDTM.toFinNDTM, Turing.EffectiveNDMachineCode, Turing.FinNDTM, Turing.FinNDTM.AcceptsWithin, Turing.NDTM.HaltsWithin, Turing.pairEncode}
For every effective code for finite-state nondeterministic Boolean machines with two
work tapes, there is a finite-state nondeterministic Boolean machine $U_N$ such that,
for each Boolean string $\alpha$, some natural number $C$ works for every Boolean string
$x$ and every natural number $t$. On input
$\langle\langle\mathrm{bits}(t),\alpha\rangle,x\rangle$, every choice sequence of length
exactly $C(t+1)$ causes $U_N$ to halt. Moreover, $U_N$ has an accepting computation of
exactly that length if and only if the machine decoded from $\alpha$ has an accepting
computation on $x$ using exactly $t$ nondeterministic choices.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Deciding bounded nondeterministic acceptance]
\lean{Turing.exists_ndAcceptsWithin_decider}
\label{Turing.exists_ndAcceptsWithin_decider}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.CodeNDTM.toFinNDTM, Turing.EffectiveNDMachineCode, Turing.FinNDTM.AcceptsWithin, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime, Turing.pairEncode}
For every effective coding scheme $c$ for nondeterministic two-work-tape machines over
the binary alphabet, there exists a finite binary-alphabet Turing machine $B$ such that,
for every binary code string $\alpha$, there is a natural-number constant $C$ with the
following property. For every binary input $x$ and every natural number $t$, if the
machine decoded from $\alpha$ accepts $x$ along some choice string of length exactly
$t$, then $B$ computes output $[1]$ on the paired encoding of the binary representation
of $t$, $\alpha$, and $x$ in exactly $C\,2^{C(t+1)}$ steps; if it does not accept in
this sense, then $B$ computes output $[0]$ on that same input in exactly $C\,2^{C(t+1)}$
steps.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Coding a Finite Nondeterministic Machine]
\lean{Turing.FinNDTM.exists_codeNDTM_accepts_linear}
\label{Turing.FinNDTM.exists_codeNDTM_accepts_linear}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.CodeNDTM, Turing.CodeNDTM.toFinNDTM, Turing.FinNDTM, Turing.FinNDTM.AcceptsWithin}
For every finite-state nondeterministic Turing machine $N$ over the binary alphabet,
there are a two-work-tape binary-choice machine $M$ with states indexed by an initial
segment of the natural numbers and a natural number $C$ such that, for every binary
input $x$ and every $t\in\mathbb{N}$, if $N$ accepts $x$ in exactly $t$ steps, then $M$
accepts $x$ in exactly $C(t+1)$ steps; conversely, if $M$ accepts $x$ in exactly $t$
steps, then $N$ accepts $x$ in some number of steps.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Nondeterministic Time Hierarchy]
\lean{Complexity.ntime_hierarchy}
\label{Complexity.ntime_hierarchy}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.NTIME, Complexity.TimeConstructible}
Let $f,g:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ be time-constructible functions: each $T\in\{f,g\}$
satisfies $n\le T(n)$ for every $n$, and some positive constant $c$ and finite
deterministic Turing machine compute the binary expansion of $T(|x|)$ on every input $x$
within $c(T(|x|)+1)$ steps. Suppose that for every natural number $A$ there is an $N$
such that, for all $n\ge N$, $A\bigl(f(n+1)+f(n)+n+1\bigr)\le g(n)$. Then
$\mathrm{NTIME}(f)$ is a proper subset of $\mathrm{NTIME}(n\mapsto g(n)+1)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Positive-Bound Nondeterministic Time Hierarchy]
\lean{Complexity.ntime_hierarchy_of_pos}
\label{Complexity.ntime_hierarchy_of_pos}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.NTIME, Complexity.TimeConstructible}
Let $f,g:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ be time-constructible functions: each $T\in\{f,g\}$
satisfies $n\le T(n)$ for every $n$, and some positive constant $c$ and finite
deterministic Turing machine compute the binary expansion of $T(|x|)$ on every input $x$
within $c(T(|x|)+1)$ steps. Suppose $g(n)>0$ for every $n$, and for every natural number
$A$ there is an $N$ such that, for all $n\ge N$, $A\bigl(f(n+1)+f(n)+n+1\bigr)\le g(n)$.
Then $\mathrm{NTIME}(f)$ is a proper subset of $\mathrm{NTIME}(g)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Strict separation of linear and quadratic time]
\lean{Complexity.NTIME_linear_ssubset_square}
\label{Complexity.NTIME_linear_ssubset_square}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.NTIME}
Among languages of binary strings, every language decidable nondeterministically within
time proportional to the input length plus one is decidable nondeterministically within
time proportional to the square of the input length plus one; moreover, some language in
the latter class is not in the former.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Universal nondeterministic machine from a setup machine]
\lean{Turing.un_universal_of_setup}
\label{Turing.un_universal_of_setup}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.CodeNDTM.toFinNDTM, Turing.EffectiveNDMachineCode, Turing.FinNDTM, Turing.FinNDTM.AcceptsWithin, Turing.FinNDTM.acceptsWithin_iff, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape, Turing.GuessRunPhase.State, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.initCfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.NDTM.HaltsWithin, Turing.NDTM.HaltsWithin.mono, Turing.NDTM.initCfg, Turing.NDTM.runWith, Turing.embedSilentTM, Turing.exists_ndInterpreterCore, Turing.guessRunTM, Turing.guessRunTM_silent_spec, Turing.pairEncode, Turing.streamStartCfg}
\difficulty{5}
For binary strings $a,b$ write $\langle a,b\rangle$ for $a$ with every bit doubled, followed by
$01$, followed by $b$; write $\mathrm{bits}(t)$ for the binary expansion of $t\in\mathbb{N}$; and
say a nondeterministic machine accepts $x$ within $t$ steps if some choice word of length exactly
$t$ leaves it halted on $x$ with output exactly $[1]$. Let $c$ be an effective code for
finite-state nondeterministic binary machines with two work tapes. Assume the following setup
property: for every $K\in\mathbb{N}$ and every tape index
$j_R<K$ there are $k\in\mathbb{N}$, an injection $\iota$ of $\{0,\dots,K-1\}$ into
$\{0,\dots,k-1\}$, a tape index outside the image of $\iota$, a deterministic $k$-work-tape
binary machine $P$ with finitely many states and a state $p_{\mathrm{exit}}$, such that for
every code $\alpha$ there is a constant $C_P$ for which, for all binary $x$ and all
$t\in\mathbb{N}$, the run of $P$ on $\langle\langle\mathrm{bits}(t),\alpha\rangle,x\rangle$
first enters $p_{\mathrm{exit}}$ after some $T_P\le C_P(t+1)$ steps, at which moment the input
head is at position $1$, all work heads are at cell $0$, the output is empty, every work tape
other than $\iota(j_R)$ is blank, and tape $\iota(j_R)$ is nonblank exactly on cells
$0,\dots,t-1$. Then there is a finite nondeterministic binary machine $U$ such that for every
code $\alpha$ some constant $C$ satisfies, for all binary $x$ and all $t$: every branch of $U$ on
$\langle\langle\mathrm{bits}(t),\alpha\rangle,x\rangle$ halts within $C(t+1)$ steps, and $U$
accepts that input within $C(t+1)$ steps if and only if the machine decoded from $\alpha$ by $c$
accepts $x$ within $t$ steps.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[One step of the bank erase]
\lean{Turing.un_bankAct}
\label{Turing.un_bankAct}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Action}
Given $k\in\mathbb{N}$, a set $S$ of work-tape indices among $\{0,\dots,k-1\}$, a guide index
$g$, a direction $m\in\{-1,0,+1\}$ and a target state $q'\in\{0,1,2\}$, this is the single
machine action that leaves the input head in place, writes a blank on every tape in $S$, moves
the heads of the tapes in $S$ and of the guide tape $g$ in direction $m$, leaves every other
tape unwritten and stationary, emits no output, and moves to state $q'$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Components of the bank erase step]
\lean{Turing.un_bankAct_eq}
\label{Turing.un_bankAct_eq}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.un_bankAct}
\difficulty{3}
Let $k\in\mathbb{N}$, let $S$ be a set of work-tape indices among $\{0,\dots,k-1\}$, let $g$ be a
guide index, $m\in\{-1,0,+1\}$ a direction and $q'\in\{0,1,2\}$ a state, and consider the bank
erase action with these parameters, which blanks the tapes in $S$, moves the tapes in $S$ and the
guide in direction $m$, and enters $q'$. Then for every tape index $i$, the action writes a blank
on tape $i$ if $i\in S$ and writes nothing otherwise, and it moves head $i$ by $m$ if $i\in S$ or
$i=g$ and by $0$ otherwise.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Guided bank erase machine]
\lean{Turing.un_bankTM}
\label{Turing.un_bankTM}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.un_bankAct}
Given $k\in\mathbb{N}$, a set $S$ of work-tape indices among $\{0,\dots,k-1\}$ and a guide index
$g$, this is the deterministic binary machine with $k$ work tapes and states $\{0,1,2\}$, starting
in state $0$. In state $0$ it unconditionally blanks the tapes in $S$ and moves them and the guide
one cell left, entering state $1$. In state $1$, if the guide tape shows a symbol it does the same
and stays in state $1$; if the guide tape shows a blank it blanks the tapes in $S$, moves them and
the guide one cell right, and enters state $2$. In state $2$ it does nothing and remains in state
$2$ forever. No step moves the input head, touches any other tape, or emits output.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Run of the guided bank erase]
\lean{Turing.un_bank_run}
\label{Turing.un_bank_run}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Action.apply_workTapes, Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.inputSymbol, Turing.Cfg.workTapeSymbols, Turing.Cfg.workTapeSymbols_eq, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape_nat, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape_of_neg, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step', Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_zero, Turing.MultiTapeTM.step, Turing.MultiTapeTM.step_of_some, Turing.moveInputPos, Turing.moveInputPos_zero, Turing.un_bankAct, Turing.un_bankAct_eq, Turing.un_bankTM, Turing.un_buffer_ge}
\difficulty{6}
Let $k\in\mathbb{N}$, let $S$ be a set of work-tape indices among $\{0,\dots,k-1\}$ and $g\notin S$
a guide index, and consider the guided bank erase machine with $k$ work tapes, states
$\{0,1,2\}$, which from state $0$ blanks the tapes in $S$ and moves them and the guide left into
state $1$, repeats this in state $1$ while the guide shows a symbol, on a blank guide cell blanks
$S$ and moves $S$ and the guide right into state $2$, and idles forever in state $2$. Let
$L\in\mathbb{N}$ and let $d$ be a configuration (on any input) in state $0$ such that, for every
$i\in S\cup\{g\}$, tape $i$ holds a binary word $w_i$ of length $L$ stored from cell $0$ (blank
elsewhere) and head $i$ is at cell $L$. Then after exactly $L+2$ steps from $d$ the machine is in
state $2$, every tape in $S$ is entirely blank, the heads of the tapes in $S\cup\{g\}$ are at
cell $0$, and every other component of $d$ (the guide's contents, all other tapes and heads,
the input head and the output) is unchanged; moreover, the state is not $2$ after any fewer than
$L+2$ steps.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Sequential composition across a relabelled seam]
\lean{Turing.un_step'}
\label{Turing.un_step'}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.mapState, Turing.Cfg.mapState_mapState, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.seamCompTM, Turing.seamCompTM_step}
\difficulty{2}
Let $M_1$ and $M_2$ be deterministic binary machines with $k$ work tapes and state sets $S_1$
(with decidable equality) and $S_2$, let $e\in S_1$ be an exit state, $s\in S_2$ an entry state
and $q_2\in S_2$ a target state, and let $M_1;M_2$ be the seam composite with state set
$S_1\sqcup S_2$, which runs $M_1$ on left states, runs $M_2$ on right states, and from the left
state $e$ takes one silent stationary step to the right state $s$. Let $g:S_0\to S_1$ be a map,
and let $c_0$, $c_2$, $c_3$ be configurations on a common input with states in $S_1$, $S_0$ and
$S_2$ respectively. Suppose that running $M_1$ from $c_0$ for $T_1$ steps gives $c_2$ with its
state relabelled by $g$, that this configuration is in state $e$, and that $M_1$ is not in state
$e$ at any earlier step; and suppose that running $M_2$ for $T_2$ steps from $c_2$ with its state
replaced by $s$ gives $c_3$, which is in state $q_2$, and that this run is not in state $q_2$ at
any earlier step. Then running $M_1;M_2$ from $c_0$ (with left-tagged state) for $T_1+1+T_2$
steps gives $c_3$ with right-tagged state, this configuration is in the right state $q_2$, and
the composite run is not in the right state $q_2$ at any earlier step.
\end{theorem}

\begin{lemma}[Any acceptance by a decider implies membership]
\lean{Complexity.nh_mem_of_accepts}
\label{Complexity.nh_mem_of_accepts}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.nh_accepts_of_halts, Turing.FinNDTM, Turing.FinNDTM.AcceptsWithin, Turing.FinNDTM.DecidesInTime, Turing.FinNDTM.decidesInTime_iff}
\difficulty{2}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic binary machine that decides a language $L$ of binary
strings within time $T:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$, meaning that on every input $x$ every choice word
of length $T(\abs{x})$ leaves $N$ halted, and $x\in L$ exactly when some such word leaves it
halted with output $[1]$. If for some binary $x$ and some $t\in\mathbb{N}$ a choice word of length
$t$ leaves $N$ halted on $x$ with output exactly $[1]$, then $x\in L$.
\end{lemma}
